concerns.text: SC-001 cites '(See US-2, US-6)' but the spec contains only three user stories (US-1 through US-3). The 'US-6' reference is dangling — either remove it or re-anchor to an existing story (US-2 already covers predictive accuracy).
SC-001 cites '(See US-2, US-6)' but the spec contains only three user stories (US-1..US-3). US-6 does not exist; the cross-reference is stale/unresolvable.

concerns.location: spec.md:US-1 Independent Test vs US-1 Acceptance Scenario 2 / FR-002
concerns.text: US-1's Independent Test requires 'exactly 50 aligned time-steps per cycle', but Acceptance Scenario 2 and FR-002 specify input shape (N_cells, 50_cycles, T_steps, 3_channels) with T_steps left as a free variable. Pick one: either T_steps is fixed at 50 or it is a resampled uniform value stated consistently.

concerns.location: spec.md:US-2 / FR-006 / SC-001 vs Key Entities
concerns.text: The prediction target is called 'final capacity fade' in US-1/FR-002/SequenceWindow.target_fade, but 'remaining useful life' in US-2 acceptance scenario 2 and 'final capacity' in BatteryCell.final_capacity. These are distinct quantities in battery literature; use one term (or explicitly define their relation) throughout.

US-2 scenario 2 attaches the R² ≥ 0.80 threshold to the unseen-protocol test set, while SC-001 frames predictive accuracy generally and SC-004 separately measures the unseen-protocol subset. Clarify whether the 0.80 threshold applies to the overall test set, the unseen-protocol subset, or both — currently the two sections imply different scopes for the same number.

'they must explicitly identify a specific subset of early-cycle features (e.g., voltage relaxation rate in cycles 10-20) as the strongest predictors' — this asserts a research OUTCOME, not a verifiable system behavior. The system cannot guarantee which features turn out strongest. Revise to a checkable deliverable: e.g., 'produce a ranked table of features with quantitative contribution scores covering all cycles/channels.'

'consistency of feature importance rankings across permutation importance and SHAP' is not measurable — no metric (e.g., rank correlation coefficient such as Spearman ρ between the two rankings) or threshold/procedure is named. State the comparison metric so met/not-met is decidable.

'exactly 50 aligned time-steps per cycle' and 'T_steps' — the uniform resampling target (T_steps value or how it is fixed) is unspecified, so the shape assertion (N, 50, T, 3) cannot be deterministically checked. Name the resampling rule or state T_steps is fixed and recorded at implementation.

Under-reach: the idea's methodology explicitly names 'permutation importance and attention mechanisms' for interpretability; the spec replaces attention with SHAP without justification. Either add attention-based attribution as an FR or record an explicit assumption that SHAP substitutes for it.

Under-reach: the idea's Expected results require 'uncertainty quantification that captures 90% of true values'. The spec only has a 'confidence_interval' attribute on ModelPrediction with no FR or SC defining how uncertainty is produced or evaluated (e.g. calibration/coverage measurement). Add an FR/SC or an explicit deferral note.

Under-reach: the idea claims identified early-cycle signatures 'outperform standard hand-crafted metrics'. No FR/SC requires a baseline comparison against hand-crafted features (e.g. incremental-capacity features), which is a core claim of the research question. Add a baseline-evaluation criterion or explicitly descope with rationale.

FR-002 says 'normalize features per cell' but does not restrict normalization statistics to the first-50-cycle window. If per-cell normalization uses statistics computed over the FULL trace (including late-life cycles), future information leaks into the early-cycle predictors, inflating R². Specify that normalization statistics are computed from the first 50 cycles only (or from training-set aggregates).

SC-003 validates 'interpretability validity' by consistency between permutation importance and SHAP. Both methods probe the SAME trained model; their agreement measures method convergence, not whether the identified signatures are scientifically valid predictors of degradation. This is a weak, near-circular validation target. Add an independent check, e.g. that top-ranked features alone (e.g. linear regression on the identified time-steps/channels) retain predictive power, or comparison against known electrochemical degradation markers.

R² ≥ 0.80 is required on a held-out set of cells with entirely unseen cycling protocols, but NASA Ames (~tens of cells) and UW datasets yield very small per-protocol cell counts. R² on a handful of held-out cells is statistically unstable and the 0.80 threshold may be unattainable for reasons of sample size rather than model quality. The spec should state a minimum held-out subset size or report uncertainty on R², and treat 0.80 as a target rather than a pass/fail gate for the unseen-protocol subset.

The target is variously called 'final capacity fade', 'remaining useful life' (US-2 Scenario 2), and 'predicted_fade'. Capacity fade (a scalar health metric) and RUL (cycles to EOL threshold) are different quantities in battery science. Define the target precisely — e.g. fade = (Q_initial − Q_final)/Q_initial at a fixed cycle count or EOL criterion — and use one term consistently.

new_concerns.text: SC-004 uses the phrasing 'aims for an R² score ≥ 0.80', which makes the success criterion optional. Replace with mandatory language (e.g., 'must achieve an R² ≥ 0.80') so the criterion is a clear, pass/fail, measurable requirement.

SC-003 defines 'interpretability validity' as a Spearman rank correlation (ρ ≥ 0.7) between permutation importance and SHAP rankings. Both metrics are derived from the same trained model, so their agreement measures methodological consistency rather than independent scientific validity. Even with the added SC-009, retaining SC-003 as a primary success criterion is circular. Reframe SC-003 as a consistency check or replace it with an external validation (e.g., correlation with known electrochemical degradation markers).
